findings.failure_scenario: A consumer looking up "England" gets "right" while looking up "United Kingdom" gets "left" — e.g., a navigation or driver-assist app keyed on this dataset configures UK users' driving side inconsistently or wrongly.
findings.summary: England is listed with driving side "right", but England drives on the left (the file itself lists United Kingdom as "left" at line 932).

findings.failure_scenario: An app routing or configuring vehicles/driving aids for Myanmar based on this record produces left/right traffic rules that contradict the country's actual left-hand traffic.
findings.summary: Myanmar is listed with driving side "right", but Myanmar has driven on the left since December 1970.

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "Scotland" returns "right" while the same file says "United Kingdom" is "left" (line 932); consumers get contradictory driving-side data for the same jurisdiction.
findings.summary: Scotland is listed with driving side "right", but Scotland (part of the UK) drives on the left.

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "Wales" returns "right" while the same file says "United Kingdom" is "left" (line 932); consumers get contradictory driving-side data for the same jurisdiction.
findings.summary: Wales is listed with driving side "right", but Wales (part of the UK) drives on the left.

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "Northern Ireland" returns "right" while the same file says "United Kingdom" is "left" (line 932); consumers get contradictory driving-side data for the same jurisdiction.
findings.summary: Northern Ireland is listed with driving side "right", but Northern Ireland (part of the UK) drives on the left.

findings.failure_scenario: Any consumer using this record for Bermuda (route planning, vehicle import rules, driver-assist configuration) is told the traffic side is right when it is left.
findings.summary: Bermuda is listed with driving side "right", but Bermuda drives on the left (British Overseas Territory with right-hand-drive vehicles).

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for the US Virgin Islands returns "right"; an app configuring driving-side-dependent behavior (e.g., lane warnings, overtaking rules) for USVI users would apply the wrong side.
findings.summary: "Virgin Islands, U.S." is listed with driving side "right", but the US Virgin Islands drive on the left (the only US jurisdiction with left-hand traffic).

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "Gibraltar" returns "left"; consumers routing or configuring vehicles for Gibraltar get the opposite of the actual right-hand traffic rule.
findings.summary: Gibraltar is listed with driving side "left", but Gibraltar uses right-hand traffic (aligned with neighboring Spain).

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "Vanuatu" returns "left"; any consumer using the record (navigation, driving-rule checks, fleet configuration) gets the wrong traffic side for the country.
findings.summary: Vanuatu is listed with driving side "left", but Vanuatu drives on the right.

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "New Caledonia" returns "left"; consumers applying French road rules (right-hand traffic) would instead be told the traffic side is left.
findings.summary: New Caledonia is listed with driving side "left", but New Caledonia (French territory) drives on the right.

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "Wallis and Futuna" returns "left"; consumers applying French road rules (right-hand traffic) get the opposite side.
findings.summary: Wallis and Futuna is listed with driving side "left", but this French territory drives on the right.

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "Falkland Islands" returns "left"; a consumer configuring driving-side-dependent behavior for the territory would apply the wrong traffic side.
findings.summary: Falkland Islands is listed with driving side "left", but the Falkland Islands are one of the few British Overseas Territories with right-hand traffic.

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "Norfolk Island" returns "right" while "Australia" (line 52) returns "left"; consumers get contradictory driving-side data for the same legal jurisdiction (Australian road rules apply).
findings.summary: Norfolk Island is listed with driving side "right", but this Australian external territory follows Australia's left-hand traffic.

findings.failure_scenario: A lookup for "British Indian Ocean Territory" returns "left"; any consumer configuring vehicles or driving rules for Diego Garcia personnel gets the wrong traffic side.
findings.summary: British Indian Ocean Territory is listed with driving side "left", but its only population (the US-UK military base on Diego Garcia) uses right-hand traffic.
